2609.24401.title: Artificial Structure Function Search: Preserving Artificial Functional Connectivity for Structured Pruning
2609.24401.paper_summary: Structured pruning is a model compression technique that is used to reduce the computational cost of deploying deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Popular methods of pruning rely on opaque heuristics or weight-based criteria that give no indication as to the structural dependencies in the network. To address these limitations we present Artificial Structure Function Search (ASF-S): a novel structured pruning framework. ASF-S utilizes Principle Gradient Importance (PGI): a novel prune-candidate selection criteria that is inspired by structure-function relationships in the brain. By ensuring the pruned structure of the model respects topographical organization of the output layer, we define Artificial Functional Connectivity (AFC) for artificial neural networks. AFC provides evidence to demonstrate that accurate smaller networks can be found using careful prune candidate selection criteria. We present results for PGI as a selection criterion and for ASF-S as a pruning framework against recent benchmarks, demonstrating that our method yields model variants with 70\% parameter reduction, that can recover baseline accuracy without re-training the pruned layers.
2609.24401.paper_summary_zh: 結構性剪枝是一種模型壓縮技術，用於減少在資源受限設備上部署深度神經網絡的計算成本。<lb/>流行的剪枝方法依賴於不透明的啟發式或基於權重的標準，這些標準無法指示網絡中的結構依賴關係。<lb/>為了解決這些限制，我們提出了人工結構函數搜索（ASF-S）：一種新穎的結構性剪枝框架。<lb/>ASF-S利用原則梯度重要性（PGI）：一種受大腦中結構-功能關係啟發的剪枝候選選擇標準。<lb/>通過確保模型的剪枝結構尊重輸出層的地形組織，我們為人工神經網絡定義了人工功能連通性（AFC）。<lb/>AFC提供證據以證明，通過仔細的剪枝候選選擇標準，可以找到準確的小型網絡。<lb/>我們展示了PGI作為選擇標準和ASF-S作為剪枝框架的結果，與最近的基準進行比較，顯示我們的方法產生的模型變體具有70\%的參數減少，且能在不重新訓練剪枝層的情況下恢復基線準確性。
